transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Head of ML, Sylvan), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead, Sylvan), Janelle Rivera (PM, Sylvan)

Summary:
Quick product demo focusing on model catalog workflows for sourcing open models, running quality+perf benches, and designing fallback/routing policies for Sylvan's regulated healthcare inference workloads. Discussed on-prem vs hosted tradeoffs, quantization compatibility, KV cache implications, and policy matrices for fallback. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Catalog export and shortlist heuristics
- Bench harnesses and expected outputs (latency, p95, token cost, quality metrics)
- Compatibility matrix columns (kernel map, quantization, memory footprint, runtime flags)
- Fallback routing: region, cheaper variant, cached prefix reuse
- Security and private deployment constraints (KMS, audit, data residency)

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'll kick off then hand to Ethan for the catalog walkthrough.
[00:14] Priya Kapoor: Hi all, Priya here. We're excited — trying to move off our current hosted endpoint because of cost and black box latency.
[00:22] Janelle Rivera: Janelle from product, just listening for rollout implications.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Liam infra. we'll be focused on network and private deploy considerations.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Great. So agenda: source open models, show how Redwood's catalog surfaces compatibility and bench signals, then talk fallback strategy and routing policies. Ethan?
[00:47] Ethan Park: Hi, thanks. I'll share my screen — walking through model-catalog UI and the CSV export. The short story: we score models across perf, cost, and quality from our curated bench runs and your own uploads.
[01:10] Ethan Park: (screen) here's a shortlist we created for healthcare-friendly models — note some are quant-ready, some need fp16 kernels. The compatibility matrix column names are: "kernel_family", "seq_len_perf_profile", "quantization_support", "kvcache_behavior", "memory_peak_mb", "fallback_variant".
[01:32] Priya Kapoor: Can you explain the kvcache behavior bit — we worry about session stickiness for chart summarization tasks.
[01:40] Ethan Park: Sure. kvcache behavior ties to how the runtime stores and reuses key/value frames — if a model has expensive KV warm-up, you might prefer prefix caching. In Redwood we have prefix caching + route-level cache keys so you can reuse for common prompts, reduces cold-start.
[01:59] Liam O'Connor: Is prefix caching compatible with private deployments? Our security team will ask.
[02:05] Maya Chen: Yes — cache is per-tenant and can be encrypted at rest. We'll include the KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[02:15] Janelle Rivera: When you say "quant-ready" what thresholds are you using? Some of our prompts are long — 1.5k tokens typical.
[02:24] Ethan Park: Good point. Quant-ready means the model runs through our quantization tests without regressing quality beyond the configured threshold. We also show a seq_len_perf_profile which predicts latency vs sequence length. For 1.5k tokens we show memory footprints and p95 latency estimates in the export.
[02:44] [04:11] Ethan Park: (narration) pulling up bench results — here is the bench CSV: columns include model_id, model_size, backbone, quant_profile, tokens_per_sec, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_est, rouge-l, exact_match, fallback_compatible.
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: The quality metrics — are those from your public bench or from our prompts?
[04:33] Ethan Park: These are our open-bench numbers. We can run a custom bench with your prompt set to give point-estimates. That's the next step we recommended.
[04:44] Maya Chen: Priya, last time you mentioned a TGI deployed baseline. We can run apples-to-apples on your 2xA10g to show delta.
[04:51] Priya Kapoor: Yep, we'll share the baseline.
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: Question on fallbacks: if primary model is busy or costs spike, can Redwood route to a smaller quantized variant automatically?
[05:05] Ethan Park: Yes — our routing policy engine supports variant fallbacks. You can define tactical policies: e.g. route by latency SLO, cost threshold, or region availability. If p95 exceeds 300ms then fallback to X-quantized-2x. There is also a quality budget to avoid unacceptable regressions.
[05:24] Janelle Rivera: Are those fallbacks per-route? We have different endpoints for triage vs production.
[05:30] Ethan Park: Per-route and per-model. And you can define canary rollout rules so a small percentage hits the fallback variant for validation.
[05:38] [08:02] Ethan Park: (screen) now looking at the compatibility matrix mapping to runtime kernels — sometimes a model's op patterns map poorly to certain kernels, so we tag recommended kernel families. That helps avoid surprise perf drop-offs on certain GPU types.
[05:53] Priya Kapoor: That kernel mapping — is it auto-detected?
[05:57] Ethan Park: It's from static analysis + microbench runs. We also run longer seq tests to detect quadratic attention hotspots.
[06:07] Liam O'Connor: What's the visibility into reproducers? If we find a perf regression we need traceability.
[06:12] Maya Chen: The console keeps a run history and you can export traces. We'll also provide the bench scripts so you can reproduce locally. Link in next steps.
[06:22] [12:19] Ethan Park: (demo) here's a sample policy: primary: model-A-8b-quant, fallback_chain: [model-A-8b-int8-small, model-B-3b-int8], triggers: [p95>350ms, cost_per_1k>threshold, region-unavailable]. Policies can be weighted and include decays to prefer higher-quality variants after transient blips.
[06:45] Priya Kapoor: For healthcare we need hard limits on regressions — can we set a max allowed quality delta (e.g., -1.5% ROUGE-L) as a hard guardrail?
[06:53] Ethan Park: Yes — you can set acceptance criteria; the routing engine will only pick fallbacks that meet the guardrail, otherwise it routes to a degraded but monitored state or returns a controlled failure.
[07:03] Janelle Rivera: What's the UX for approving candidate fallbacks? Our product folks need to sign off.
[07:08] Ethan Park: There's a candidate review flow — you can run offline A/B on recorded prompts and then approve a fallback chain. We keep diffs and sample outputs for review.
[07:17] [20:46] Priya Kapoor: Security question: how is data residency enforced on Dedicated vs Private deployments? We can't have PHI cross regions.
[07:27] Maya Chen: For Dedicated you can restrict regions and pin capacity to a region. For Private (VPC/on-prem) all processing stays inside your network. We support KMS/HSM integrations for key control and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
[07:42] Liam O'Connor: What about egress from our VPC to fetch model shards — we need to understand network flows.
[07:47] Ethan Park: In the Private package you either bring the model artifacts locally (air-gapped) or we provision within your private subnet with no public egress — we'll provide the network checklist.
[07:57] Priya Kapoor: Bench outputs — can we compute quality vs cost curves to pick an operating point?
[08:05] Ethan Park: Absolutely. The Optimize view visualizes cost per quality point; you can choose a knee point and export policy recommendations.
[08:13] Janelle Rivera: Suppose we pick model-C for production but we see periodic traffic spikes — can we configure burst capacity on Dedicated?
[08:20] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity and auto-scaling policies. We'll size proposals based on your 95th percentile.
[08:28] [28:55] Ethan Park: (demo) walking through an export: CSV + JSON manifest, fields include: model_hash, build_flags, runtime_flags, suggested_quant_profile, fallback_variants, bench_summary_link. We also include human notes from our model onboarding engineers.
[08:48] Priya Kapoor: About quant profiles — are they deterministic across runs? Does retraining or small tokenizer changes affect them?
[08:55] Ethan Park: Tokenizer changes can change tokenization patterns; we recommend re-running the bench if tokenization or prompt engineering changes substantially. Quant profiles are stable for the binary but depend on sequence length distribution.
[09:07] Liam O'Connor: If we need on-prem, how long does provisioning take?
[09:12] Maya Chen: Typical Private deployment in an enterprise setting is 3-6 weeks depending on security review; air-gapped or HSM integrations add extra time.
[09:21] [37:10] Ethan Park: (walkthrough) here's a real example from another customer: primary 7b fp16, fallback to 7b int8-small with a 4% rouge drop but 40% cost reduction. They used canary at 5% then rolled to 100% after review. We can anonymize that case study for Sylvan.
[09:45] Priya Kapoor: That 4% drop is too big for some of our tasks. We need the system to auto-reject fallbacks that cross our per-route thresholds.
[09:53] Ethan Park: We can do that; set an explicit "quality_floor" per endpoint.
[09:59] Janelle Rivera: What's the signal used to measure quality in real-time? We don't want human labeling in production.
[10:05] Ethan Park: We support synthetic prompt-based monitors and embedding drift metrics plus a small human-in-the-loop sampling for edge cases. You plug in your evaluation keys for privacy.
[10:14] [45:30] Priya Kapoor: If we run the bench internally, can we upload results back to Redwood for consolidated catalog scoring?
[10:36] Ethan Park: Yes — there's a "customer bench upload" feature; we ingest and merge signals to the catalog but keep your data private — it won't be used in public aggregates without permission.
[10:47] Liam O'Connor: One more infra nit: does Redis get used for KV store? We prefer not to introduce new hosted infra.
[10:54] Ethan Park: The runtime can use a variety of backends; for Private we can configure it to use your managed Redis or a local in-memory store. We'll document the options.
[11:03] Maya Chen: Ok, let's recap and owners.
[11:07] (recap) Maya Chen: Redwood to share catalog export + bench scripts and SOC2/security pack. Ethan to run perf bench against Sylvan baseline and return numbers. Priya to provide prompt sets. Liam to share network diagram. Schedule on-prem deep dive.
[11:27] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Appreciate the demo — lots to digest.
[11:31] Janelle Rivera: Thanks, team.
[11:33] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via CRM with the artifacts.
